inferences: The step count carries one search's work into the next: a frame's searches stop being answered once it reaches 3,000, so where retail counts its steps is something a game sees.
The dropped travel-time query builds the routing cache towards the enemy's area and counts against the frame's routing updates, so it can defer a later route query in the same frame.
The game's answers last one search; the source area is not marked as reached and can be a candidate.
beforeThisChange: returned once it had taken 3,000 steps, counting each link before its tests and none at the queue (census)
measured the distance limit to the area's waypoint, and only for a positive limit (census)
refused a step whose measured point lay within 40 units of the enemy (census)
asked the game nothing about a candidate and kept no store of answers (census)
set up its start record before asking about the start, refusing area 0 without asking (census)
had no rule against passing near the enemy or heading more than halfway towards it
charged an approach to the enemy at any distance
charged nothing for an occupied area
skipped an area reached again in equal time and stored a time after its costs
kept its best area when it reached it again
